chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Same band back from South America; Lyons has him stand up and stop playing
summary: Back in New York with Jerry Blake and Doc Cheatham, he takes Lyons's advice to conduct standing up and loses his piano chops.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: So that brings -- we have already covered what happened after that.
You went to South America. So let's get back to, I think it was 1927, when you came back to New York.
And you went into vaudeville. Now, when the band came back to New York from South America, did you disband, or did you keep the same band.
Well, we kept the same band, with one or two changes. Some of the boys didn't want to travel anymore, you know?

So they were replaced. And so now, we got fellows like Jerry Blake, Doc Cheatham. And a queer thing happened to me which I had no business to agree to at that time. And I'm warning all young pianists, don't agree to that anymore. He said, Arthur Lyons said to me, 'Now, the big band leaders now are not playing.' 'They take the baton and stand up.' You know. So, I agreed with him because I didn't want to work no more than I had to work. See, I never did care much for work.

So I agreed with him and I stood up. And from then on, by travelling, I never got any chance to practice. And I began to get rusty on my instrument. After awhile, I just cut out the solos. You see, altogether. And just went on, which was pretty good, as a band conductor standing up.
